# cache

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/cache"
```

Package cache is the public facade for the SDK's caching, and it offers two surfaces because there are two different jobs.

### The primitive: Cache\[K,V]

[Cache](#Cache) is a generic LRU + TTL map — construct it, Set, Fetch, done. No port, no error surface, no vocabulary. Reach for it when you want a bounded map with expiry inside one component.

```
c := cache.New[string, int](cache.Config[string, int]{MaxEntries: 1024, DefaultTTL: time.Minute})
c.Set("answer", 42)
v, ok := c.Fetch("answer") // 42, true
```

### The domain: Store\[V]

[Store](#Store) is the cache as an INTERFACE, with the three things a primitive deliberately does not have: invalidation by tag, protection against a stampede of concurrent misses, and the ability to put one store in front of another. Reach for it when a cache is part of your architecture rather than an implementation detail — when something else has to be able to invalidate what you cached, or when the thing behind the cache must not be hit N times the instant a hot key expires.

```
store, err := cache.NewMemory[Profile](cache.MemoryConfig{
    MaxEntries: 10_000,       // refused if zero — a capacity is your decision
    DefaultTTL: time.Minute,
})

loader, _ := store.(cache.Loader[Profile])
profile, err := loader.Load(ctx, key, func(ctx context.Context) (cache.Entry[Profile], error) {
    p, err := db.Profile(ctx, id)
    return cache.Entry[Profile]{Value: p, TTL: time.Minute, Tags: []string{"user:" + id}}, err
})

tagger, _ := store.(cache.Tagger)
removed, err := tagger.InvalidateTag(ctx, "user:"+id) // every entry derived from that user
```

The two do not compete: the domain store is BUILT on the primitive, and [Cache](#Cache) stays exactly what it was.

### Fetch, not Get — on both surfaces

A hit promotes the entry in the recency order and moves the counters, so a read MUTATES. Naming it Get would promise a purity neither surface offers, and in the domain store it takes a write lock for precisely that reason.

### Stampede protection stops at the process boundary

[Loader](#Loader).Load guarantees ONE fill per key across every goroutine in THIS process. It does not coordinate across replicas. Ten instances of a service each running this still send ten concurrent requests to the origin when a hot key expires — so a fleet's worst-case origin load falls by the concurrency factor within an instance, not to one. Cross-process collapsing needs a shared lease, which is a distributed system and not something a cache can promise. Size the origin against the number of replicas, not against the number of requests.

[Leaser](#Leaser).LoadLeased takes that lease, from a lock.Locker the processes share — the lock domain's file locker on one machine. Over a chain whose far tier every process reaches, the origin then sees one fill per key; over a memory store alone, which shares no value, the processes only take turns, one fill at a time.

### Nothing across tiers is atomic

[NewChain](#NewChain) is two independent stores, and there is no transaction between them. Every multi-tier operation has a window in which they disagree; the package chooses which side of that window is safer and says so, rather than implying a consistency it cannot deliver. See internal/service/data/cache's CLAUDE.md for each choice and its reason.

## Constants

<a name="NoExpiry"></a>
```go
const NoExpiry time.Duration = -1
```

NoExpiry is the [Entry](#Entry).TTL that stores an entry with no deadline.

It is deliberately distinct from the zero TTL, which means "use the store's default". A store with a one-minute default holding one entry that must never expire is a real combination, and reading both meanings out of 0 would make the second one unsayable.

Initialised with `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/cache.NoExpiry`.

<a name="PolicyLRU"></a>
```go
const PolicyLRU Policy = 0
```

PolicyLRU evicts the least-recently-used entry. It is the zero Policy.

Initialised with `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/kernel/collections/cache.PolicyLRU`.

<a name="PolicyS3FIFO"></a>
```go
const PolicyS3FIFO Policy = 1
```

PolicyS3FIFO admits new keys into a small probationary queue and keeps the ones hit there in a main one, so a one-time scan does not flush the hot set.

Initialised with `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/kernel/collections/cache.PolicyS3FIFO`.

<a name="FillFailed"></a>
```go
var FillFailed *errs.Error
```

FillFailed is returned by Load when your fill fails and its error carries no SDK code of its own. Nothing is stored: caching a failure turns one bad minute at the origin into a full TTL of confident wrong answers.

Initialised with `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/cache.CacheFillFailed`.

Code `0.2.18.3` · reason `CACHE_FILL_FAILED` · public "The cache fill function failed and nothing was stored"

<a name="LeaseFailed"></a>


LeaseFailed is returned by LoadLeased when its locker could not answer: the lease on the key could be neither taken nor given up.

<a name="Absent"></a>
## func [Absent](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/cache/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Absent(cause error, ttl time.Duration) error
```

Absent marks a fill's failure as an answer to cache: the key does not exist at the origin. A store's Load keeps a negative entry for ttl and returns the same error — errors.Is still finds cause — without calling the fill again. A ttl that is not positive caches nothing.

<a name="NewChain"></a>
## func [NewChain](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/cache/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func NewChain[V any](cfg ChainConfig, tiers ...Store[V]) (store Store[V], err error)
```

NewChain puts each store in front of the next: tiers\[0] is consulted first, the last is the authority. A hit in a far tier is promoted into every nearer one, carrying its REMAINING TTL and its tags.

Every tier must implement [EntryFetcher](#EntryFetcher) and [Tagger](#Tagger), checked here and refused rather than discovered per call: a value promoted without its tags is one [Tagger](#Tagger) can no longer reach, so an invalidation would report success while a nearer tier kept serving the entry.

<a name="NewMemory"></a>
## func [NewMemory](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/cache/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func NewMemory[V any](cfg MemoryConfig) (store Store[V], err error)
```

NewMemory builds an in-process store: an LRU with TTL, a tag index, and stampede protection on Load.

The returned [Store](#Store) also implements [EntryFetcher](#EntryFetcher), [Tagger](#Tagger) and [Loader](#Loader).

A non-positive MaxEntries is REFUSED, not defaulted. A capacity is the whole statement of how much memory you are willing to spend, so any number chosen for you would be arbitrary — and the value a zero would naturally mean, unbounded, is the dangerous one.

NewWeighedMemory builds an in-process store bounded by MaxBytes as well as MaxEntries, each value measured by weigh when it is stored. An entry heavier than a stripe's share of MaxBytes is refused at Set.

<a name="Cache.Delete"></a>
### func \(Cache\) [Delete](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/kernel/collections/cache/cache.go>)

```go
func (*Cache) Delete(key K)
```

Delete removes key if present. An explicit Delete does NOT fire OnEvict (that hook is for capacity/expiry removals only).

<a name="Cache.Expire"></a>
### func \(Cache\) [Expire](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/kernel/collections/cache/cache.go>)

```go
func (*Cache) Expire() int
```

Expire removes every entry whose deadline has passed and reports how many it removed. Each counts as an eviction and reaches OnEvict after the lock is released, as a lazy expiry does. The cache starts no goroutine: the caller decides when, and how often, to call it — on a ticker of its own, or on its scheduler. It costs O(k log n) for k expired entries; an entry without a deadline costs nothing, and a cache without any reads no clock.

<a name="Cache.Fetch"></a>
### func \(Cache\) [Fetch](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/kernel/collections/cache/cache.go>)

```go
func (*Cache) Fetch(key K) (value V, ok bool)
```

Fetch returns the value for key and whether it was present and unexpired. A hit promotes the entry to most-recently-used (hence Fetch, not a pure Get).

<a name="Cache.Keys"></a>
### func \(Cache\) [Keys](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/kernel/collections/cache/cache.go>)

```go
func (*Cache) Keys() iter.Seq[K]
```

Keys yields the keys present and unexpired when the loop starts, in no particular order. They are copied under the lock and yielded after it is released, so the loop's body may call the cache — Set, Delete, Fetch — without deadlocking; what the body changes is not seen by the loop. A walk is not a read: no entry is promoted and no counter moves. Each loop allocates one slice of the keys.

```go
type ChainConfig = svccache.ChainConfig
```

ChainConfig is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/data/cache.ChainConfig`, declared as:

```go
type ChainConfig struct {
	// OnPromoteError, if non-nil, is called when a value served from a FAR
	// tier could not be written into a nearer one.
	//
	// A failed promotion is not a failed read: the caller already has the
	// value, and failing the call would turn a degraded cache into a degraded
	// service. But it is also not nothing — a near tier that rejects every
	// promotion is a tier that will never be used again, and with this hook nil
	// that is completely invisible. Wire it.
	OnPromoteError func(key string, err error)
	// Clock is what LoadLeased waits on between two reads while another
	// process holds a key's lease. nil means clock.System. Nothing else in
	// the chain reads time: every tier keeps its own clock.
	Clock          clock.Timed
	// LeasePoll is how often LoadLeased reads the chain again while another
	// process holds a key's lease. 0 means 25ms, the file locker's own poll;
	// negative is refused.
	LeasePoll      time.Duration
}
```

<a name="Config"></a>
## type [Config](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/cache/gen_facade.go>)

Config is the public alias for the primitive's constructor configuration.

```go
type Config[K comparable, V any] = kcache.Config[K, V]
```

Config is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/kernel/collections/cache.Config`, declared as:

```go
type Config[K comparable, V any] struct {
	// MaxEntries caps the live entry count (LRU eviction above it). 0 = unbounded.
	MaxEntries int
	// DefaultTTL applies to Set entries (SetTTL overrides per-entry). 0 = no expiry.
	DefaultTTL time.Duration
	// Clock is the time source (injectable for tests). nil = clock.System.
	Clock      clock.Clock
	// OnEvict, if non-nil, is called with the key+value of every entry removed by
	// capacity eviction or expiry (not by an explicit Delete/Set-overwrite).
	OnEvict    func(key K, val V)
	// MaxWeight caps the summed weight of the live entries, evicting above it as
	// MaxEntries does; both apply when both are set. 0 = unbounded. An entry
	// heavier than MaxWeight alone is stored and evicts every other entry: the
	// primitive has no error to refuse it with.
	MaxWeight  int64
	// WeightOf, if non-nil, weighs an entry when it is stored; a negative answer
	// counts as 0, and one above math.MaxInt32 as math.MaxInt32. nil = every
	// entry weighs 1, so MaxWeight is then a count.
	WeightOf   func(key K, val V) int64
	// Policy chooses the victim when the cache is full. The zero value is
	// PolicyLRU.
	Policy     Policy
}
```

Entry is what a caller stores: the value, its lifetime, and the tags by which it can later be invalidated in bulk.

Entry is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/cache.EntryValue`, declared as:

```go
type Entry[V any] struct {
	// Value is the payload.
	Value V
	// TTL is how long the entry stays fetchable.
	//
	//   > 0        this exact lifetime
	//   0          the store's configured default
	//   [NoExpiry] no deadline at all
	//
	// Any other negative value is a mistake, not a third meaning, and is
	// refused with [CacheEntryRejected] rather than reinterpreted.
	TTL   time.Duration
	// Tags label the entry for bulk invalidation. Order is not significant and
	// duplicates are collapsed. An empty tag is refused: it names a set nobody
	// can ask for, so accepting it would index the entry under a key that can
	// only ever be reached by accident.
	//
	// Tags cost memory in the store's reverse index — see
	// internal/service/data/cache/CLAUDE.md, which states the per-pair cost and
	// measures it.
	Tags  []string
}
```

<a name="EntryFetcher.FetchEntry"></a>
### func \(EntryFetcher\) [FetchEntry](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/cache/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (EntryFetcher) FetchEntry(ctx context.Context, key string) (EntryValue[V], bool, error)
```

FetchEntry is [Store.Fetch](#Store.Fetch) returning the stored entry — value, remaining TTL and tags. It mutates the store for the same reasons Fetch does.

The TTL it reports is the REMAINING time, not the one originally supplied: promoting an entry with its original TTL would extend its life every time it moved between tiers.

<a name="Leaser"></a>
## type [Leaser](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/cache/gen_facade.go>)

Leaser is the sibling that carries stampede protection across processes: on a miss it takes a lease named after the key from a lock.Locker the processes share, so one of them fills while the others wait for its value. A memory store alone shares no value: there the lease only takes turns, one fill at a time.

```go
type Leaser[V any] = corecache.Leaser[V]
```

Leaser is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/cache.Leaser`, declared as:

```go
type Leaser[V any] interface {
	LoadLeased(ctx context.Context, key string, fill Fill[V], locker lock.Locker) (V, error)
}
```

<a name="Leaser.LoadLeased"></a>
### func \(Leaser\) [LoadLeased](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/cache/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Leaser) LoadLeased(ctx context.Context, key string, fill Fill[V], locker lock.Locker) (V, error)
```

LoadLeased is Load with a lease named "cache:" + key taken from locker on a miss, after the in-process collapse. The holder reads the store again, fills, stores and releases. A process that finds the lease held fills nothing: it reads the store again every poll step of the store's clock until the holder's value lands or its own ctx ends — or until the lease comes free without a value (the holder failed, died, or let a lease that can expire lapse), when it takes the lease and reads once more before filling. A nil locker makes it Load. A locker that cannot answer fails the call with \[CacheLeaseFailed]. A lease that can expire is not renewed during the fill: its lifetime must outlast the fill.

<a name="Loader"></a>
## type [Loader](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/cache/gen_facade.go>)

Loader is the sibling that fills a miss while collapsing concurrent misses on one key into a single fill — within one process, and not across replicas. See the package documentation before sizing an origin against it.

```go
type Loader[V any] = corecache.Loader[V]
```

Loader is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/cache.Loader`, declared as:

```go
type Loader[V any] interface {
	Load(ctx context.Context, key string, fill Fill[V]) (V, error)
}
```

<a name="Loader.Load"></a>
### func \(Loader\) [Load](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/cache/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Loader) Load(ctx context.Context, key string, fill Fill[V]) (V, error)
```

Load returns the value for key, calling fill exactly once across all concurrent callers of this key in this process if the cache does not hold it. A fill that fails stores nothing and returns \[CacheFillFailed] — unless the failure already carries an SDK code, in which case it propagates untouched (ADR 0005 §origin wins).

fill does NOT receive ctx. It receives the shared call's context: the first caller's values with every deadline removed, cancelled only once every waiting caller has gone. A caller whose own ctx ends while it waits gets its own ctx.Err() and leaves the fill running for the others.

<a name="MemoryConfig"></a>
## type [MemoryConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/cache/gen_facade.go>)

MemoryConfig parameterises [NewMemory](#NewMemory). Its zero value is NOT a working cache — MaxEntries must be stated, and is refused rather than defaulted.

```go
type MemoryConfig = svccache.MemoryConfig
```

MemoryConfig is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/data/cache.MemoryConfig`, declared as:

```go
type MemoryConfig struct {
	// MaxEntries caps the live entry count; the least-recently-used entry is
	// evicted above it. It MUST be positive.
	MaxEntries int
	// DefaultTTL applies to every entry whose own TTL is zero. Zero means the
	// default is "no deadline", so entries leave only by eviction, by Delete,
	// or by tag invalidation. Negative is refused.
	DefaultTTL time.Duration
	// Clock is the time source, injectable so TTL is testable. nil means
	// clock.System. Only the reading half of the port is required — a cache
	// reads time (ADR 0039); LoadLeased alone waits, on Clock when it can wait
	// (clock.System, a clock.ManualClock) and on clock.System otherwise. A
	// clock.CoarseClock makes a TTL'd hit's clock read an atomic load, and
	// every expiry late by up to its resolution.
	Clock      clock.Clock
	// Stripes splits the store into independent stripes, each with its own
	// lock, its own share of MaxEntries and MaxBytes and its own tag index, so
	// goroutines working on keys of different stripes never wait for one
	// another. 0 means 1, one store as before; above MaxEntries (or a positive
	// MaxBytes) it is held there, and above 1024 at 1024. Negative is refused.
	Stripes    int
	// MaxBytes bounds the summed weight of the live values, as measured by the
	// weigher handed to [NewWeighedMemory]; entries are evicted above it as
	// above MaxEntries, both bounds applying. 0 means no byte bound. An entry
	// heavier than one stripe's share of it is refused with
	// CACHE_ENTRY_REJECTED at Set. Negative is refused, and so is a positive
	// MaxBytes given to [NewMemory], which has no weigher to measure it with.
	MaxBytes   int64
	// Policy is the eviction policy: least recently used (the zero), or
	// S3-FIFO, which keeps a hot set through a scan.
	Policy     kcache.Policy
	// LeasePoll is how often LoadLeased reads the store again while another
	// process holds a key's lease. 0 means 25ms, the file locker's own poll;
	// negative is refused.
	LeasePoll  time.Duration
}
```

## type [Refresher](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/cache/gen_facade.go>)

Refresher is the sibling that refreshes a hot entry before it expires: the value is served from the cache while one background fill replaces it.

```go
type Refresher[V any] = corecache.Refresher[V]
```

Refresher is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/cache.Refresher`, declared as:

```go

	LoadRefreshing(ctx context.Context, key string, fill Fill[V], before time.Duration) (V, error)
```

<a name="Refresher.LoadRefreshing"></a>
### func \(Refresher\) [LoadRefreshing](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/cache/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Refresher) LoadRefreshing(ctx context.Context, key string, fill Fill[V], before time.Duration) (V, error)
```

LoadRefreshing is Load, except on a hit whose remaining lifetime is below before: the value is returned at once and ONE background fill per key starts, on the caller's context values without its cancellation, bounded by the entry's remaining lifetime; what it returns replaces the entry, and a failure leaves the entry to expire. A hit outside that window starts nothing. A before that is not positive is refused with \[CacheMisconfigured].

<a name="Store"></a>
## type [Store](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/cache/gen_facade.go>)

Store is the cache port: Fetch, Set, Delete.

The method set is FROZEN at three. New capabilities arrive as SIBLING interfaces you reach by type assertion — [EntryFetcher](#EntryFetcher), [Tagger](#Tagger) and [Loader](#Loader) — because this alias publishes the interface, Go interfaces are structural, and a fourth method would break every downstream implementer at compile time with no deprecation window.

```go

```

Store is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/cache.Store`, declared as:

```go
type Store[V any] interface {
	Delete(ctx context.Context, key string) error
	Fetch(ctx context.Context, key string) (V, bool, error)
	Set(ctx context.Context, key string, entry EntryValue[V]) error
}
```

<a name="Store.Delete"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Delete](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/cache/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Store) Delete(ctx context.Context, key string) error
```

Delete removes key. It is idempotent: deleting a key that names nothing reports nil, because a caller who wanted it gone has got what they asked for.

<a name="Store.Fetch"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Fetch](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/cache/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Store) Fetch(ctx context.Context, key string) (V, bool, error)
```

Fetch returns the value stored under key and whether it was present and unexpired. It MUTATES the store — recency, counters, lazy expiry — which is why it is not called Get. A miss is (zero, false, nil), never an error: a cache that does not hold something has done nothing wrong.

<a name="Store.Set"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Set](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/cache/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Store) Set(ctx context.Context, key string, entry EntryValue[V]) error
```

Set stores entry under key, replacing whatever was there. An empty key, an empty tag, or a negative TTL that is not [NoExpiry](#NoExpiry) is refused with \[CacheEntryRejected] rather than stored.
